bib.title: PLAN-AND-ACT: Improving Planning of Agents for Long-Horizon Tasks

read.skipped: Reference list (skimmed for lineage only); appendix prompts read, repetitive guideline blocks skimmed.

question: Can separating a fine-tuned PLANNER from an EXECUTOR, with synthetic plan data and dynamic replanning, improve LLM web agents on long-horizon tasks?
hypothesis: Explicit planning bridges the gap between high-level user intent and low-level actions, and off-the-shelf LLMs plan poorly without training on grounded plan data.
contributions: A framework separating a PLANNER (structured high-level plans) from an EXECUTOR (environment-specific actions) for long-horizon tasks.
A synthetic data pipeline: grounded plan generation from action trajectories (Sec 4.2) and synthetic plan expansion (Sec 4.3), without manual annotation or a sandbox for the expansion step.
State-of-the-art results on WebArena-Lite (57.58% final) and text-only WebVoyager (81.36%).

method.summary: A PLANNER LLM turns the user query into a step-by-step plan and replans after every EXECUTOR action; the EXECUTOR maps plan plus HTML to a web action. Both are fine-tuned (SFT) on synthetic data: GPT-4o annotates successful trajectories with grounded plans, expands plans to 10,000 query-plan pairs, adds 5,000 targeted by failure analysis, and a teacher adds CoT traces.

results.claim: Full PLAN-AND-ACT (finetuned planner, synthetic data, dynamic replanning, CoT) reaches a new state-of-the-art success rate on WebArena-Lite.
results.setup: WebArena-Lite, LLaMA-3.3-70B planner and executor finetuned on WebArena-Lite plus synthetic trajectories, plans, replanning and CoT data
results.table: Table 1, row + CoT (PLAN-AND-ACT), column + Synthetic Traj.
results.quote: a state-of-the-art 57.58% success rate on the WebArena-Lite benchmark

results.claim: Text-only WebVoyager SOTA with a QwQ-32B Plan-and-Act model.
results.setup: WebVoyager, QwQ-32B finetuned on 1500 synthetic trajectories, QwQ-32B annotated plans, CoT and 10k synthetic plans
results.quote: text-only state-of-the-art 81.36% success rate on WebVoyager

results.claim: A base, un-finetuned executor with no planner scores 9.85; adding the best static planner lifts it to 29.63.
results.setup: WebArena-Lite, base prompted LLaMA-3.3-70B executor, planner finetuned with plan expansion and targeted augmentation
results.quote: Even with a base EXECUTOR, adding a PLANNER increases success rate from 9.85% to 29.63%.

results.claim: Dynamic replanning raises the finetuned-executor result from 43.63 to 53.94, surpassing WebRL.
results.setup: WebArena-Lite, + Synthetic Traj. executor, planner with replanning data (LoRA fine-tune)
results.table: Table 1, row + Dynamic Replanning, column + Synthetic Traj.
results.quote: significantly increases the performance of the model by 10.31%
results.note: Abstract/Intro-level text states 53.94% as the SOTA in the contribution list, while the abstract states 57.58% (after CoT). Text says it surpasses WebRL by 4.84% (53.94 - 49.1).

results.claim: With a base executor, dynamic replanning alone gives 44.24 versus 9.85 without a planner.

limits: Action trajectory generation depends on a baseline model that can already complete the web tasks; benchmarks without training data (WebVoyager) need such a base model.
Dynamic replanning after every action is inefficient and slow; authors propose letting the EXECUTOR decide when to replan or delegating to subagents.
Single runs; no seeds, variance or significance tests reported; no latency or cost numbers for replanning.
Only web navigation tested; broader digital environments, multimodal inputs, RL plan optimisation and memory are future work.
Code, weights and data are not stated as released; LoRA hyperparameters and trajectory counts for the plan/replan/CoT sets are not given.
WebArena-Lite training data used to tune and evaluate the same sites; Table 1 baselines marked * are copied from WebRL.

figures.caption: PLAN-AND-ACT System Diagram. Given the initial user query, the PLANNER breaks it down into a high-level plan, which is given to the EXECUTOR which uses the plan to guide its actions. Once the action has been taken and the HTML changes, the PLANNER dynamically generates a new plan.
